## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, mixOmics, dplyr, tidyr, purrr, ggplot2, patchwork, writexl)
here::i_am("07_Multivariate/01_pca/a_script/01_pca.qmd")
```

## Read proteins

`proteins` holds the normalised log2 abundances of 3,042 proteins in 131 samples, with the blood
index's effect removed (`proteins_adjusted.rds`), and the sample table.

```{r read}
stage <- here("07_Multivariate", "01_pca")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins_adjusted.rds"))
targets <- proteins$targets
gene_of <- set_names(proteins$genes$Genes, rownames(proteins))
dim(proteins$E)
```

## Remove each participant's mean

Participant explains about half of the first MDS coordinate in `02_Quantification`, so a plain
PCA mostly separates people. `pca(multilevel = participant)` first subtracts each participant's
mean profile (Liquet et al. 2012, doi:10.1186/1471-2105-13-325), leaving only how a person's four
samples differ from one another: training, leg and noise. Proteins stay unscaled, as in the MDS
plot.

```{r pca}
components <- pca(t(proteins$E), ncomp = 10, multilevel = targets$participant)
variance <- tibble(
  component = names(components$prop_expl_var$X),
  proportion = unname(components$prop_expl_var$X)
)
variance
```

## What drives the components

For the first four components, the share of each component's variance that timepoint, treatment
and group explain, from a linear model on each factor.

```{r structure}
scores <- as_tibble(components$variates$X[, 1:5], rownames = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(targets, by = "sample_id")
pc_structure <- expand_grid(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4), factor = c("timepoint", "treatment", "group")
) |>
  mutate(r_squared = map2_dbl(component, factor, function(pc, f) {
    summary(lm(scores[[pc]] ~ scores[[f]]))$r.squared
  }))
pivot_wider(pc_structure, names_from = factor, values_from = r_squared) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3)))
```

## Figure

Samples on the first two components, coloured by arm, open before training and filled after. A
line joins each leg's two samples, so its direction is that leg's training change. The bars give
the 20 proteins with the largest loadings on each component, the weight each carries in the
component score.

```{r figure}
#| fig-height: 10
arm_colours <- c(BFR = "#D55E00", HLRT = "#0072B2")
pc_label <- function(pc) sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", pc, 100 * components$prop_expl_var$X[[pc]])

score_plot <- scores |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg, sep = "_")) |>
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = leg_id), alpha = 0.35, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = timepoint), size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = arm_colours) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(T1 = 1, T2 = 16)) +
  labs(x = pc_label("PC1"), y = pc_label("PC2"), colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)

pc_loadings <- as_tibble(components$loadings$X[, 1:2], rownames = "protein") |>
  mutate(gene = gene_of[protein])

loading_plot <- function(pc) {
  pc_loadings |>
    slice_max(abs(.data[[pc]]), n = 20) |>
    ggplot(aes(.data[[pc]], reorder(gene, .data[[pc]]), fill = .data[[pc]] > 0)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey30", `FALSE` = "grey65")) +
    labs(x = paste(pc, "loading"), y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 8)
}

pca_page <- score_plot / (loading_plot("PC1") | loading_plot("PC2")) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.2, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Multilevel PCA: samples with each participant's mean removed")
pca_page

pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "01_pca.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
print(pca_page)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

```{r write}
write_xlsx(
  list(
    variance = variance,
    structure = pc_structure,
    scores = select(scores, sample_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, PC1:PC5),
    loadings = as_tibble(components$loadings$X[, 1:5], rownames = "protein") |>
      mutate(gene = gene_of[protein], .after = protein)
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "01_pca.xlsx")
)
```
